lessons.title: Transport
lessons.scenario: You are in Sam's garage with Smarty and Mia. Sam has a motorbike, a suitcase and some toy vehicles. Talk about ways to travel.

items.note: Say "train" for a long vehicle that runs on a track. You can say: I go by train.

image.describe: A big colourful train with a few carriages on a railway track; Smarty the black cat waves from a window.

items.example: The plane is in the sky.
items.note: A plane flies in the sky. You can say: I go by plane.

image.describe: A white passenger plane flying in a blue sky with a few clouds; Smarty the black cat looks out of a round window.

items.example: The boat is on the water.
items.note: A boat goes on the water. You can say: I go by boat.

image.describe: A small blue and white boat on calm water with Smarty the black cat wearing a little sailor hat on deck.

items.note: A motorbike has two wheels and an engine.

image.describe: A shiny red motorbike parked in a garage; Smarty the black cat sits on the seat.

items.note: You put your things in a suitcase when you travel.

image.describe: A big blue suitcase with wheels standing open next to Smarty the black cat.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A boat goes on the water. A train goes on a track.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the first word after The: train.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence about how you go.
practice.explanation: Say by + the vehicle to tell how you go.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its plural.
practice.explanation: Add -s to talk about more than one.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You can ride a motorbike. You cannot ride a suitcase or the sky.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: The plane is in the sky.
practice.answer: The plane is in the sky.
practice.explanation: A plane flies in the sky.

practice.prompt: You travel. Which one do you carry with your things?
practice.explanation: You carry a suitcase. A train or a boat carries you.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the vehicle and the colour.

practice.prompt: Smarty has a blue suitcase. Which sentence is right?
practice.explanation: The sentence must use the colour blue.

story.hook: Which toy vehicle does Smarty like?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have a train, a plane and a boat, too.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The train is red. The boat is blue.

questions.explanation: Sam says the train is red and the boat is blue.
Smarty says: I like the boat.
Mia says: The plane is big!

image.describe: A garage with a red motorbike and a blue suitcase. Sam shows toy models of a train, a plane and a boat on a table to Mia and Smarty the black cat.

mission.setup: You are in Sam's garage with Smarty and Mia. Sam has a motorbike, a suitcase and some toy vehicles. Talk about ways to travel.

turns.smarty: How do you go to school?
turns.hint: Say I go by + a vehicle, or I go on foot.

turns.smarty: I like the train. Do you like trains?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not. You can also say what you like.

turns.smarty: I have a suitcase. What colour is it?
turns.hint: Say a colour. For example: It is blue.

lessons.title: January to May
lessons.scenario: Mia, Sam and Smarty look at pictures of the year. Talk about the first months and what you like.

items.note: January is the first month of the year.
February comes after January.
March comes after February.
April comes after March.
May comes after April. Months start with a capital letter in English.

practice.prompt: Which month comes in the middle?
practice.explanation: The order is January, February, March.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the month at the end.

practice.prompt: Put the months in order.
practice.explanation: The order is March, April, May.

practice.prompt: Match each month with the month that comes next.
practice.explanation: Months have a fixed order. Each one has a next month.

practice.prompt: Which month comes after April?
practice.explanation: April comes before May.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Say it slowly: It rains in April.

practice.prompt: Type a month you like.
practice.explanation: Any of these months can fit. You can say what you like.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for windy and for March.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: It snows in February. Snow comes with cold weather.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I like March. It is windy.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I love May. It is warm and sunny.

questions.explanation: Sam says: I like March.

questions.prompt: Which month is warm and sunny?
questions.explanation: Mia says May is warm and sunny.
Mia says: It snows in February.

image.describe: A classroom table with five big pictures in a row: a snowy day, a windy day, a rainy day and a warm sunny day. Mia, Sam and Smarty the black cat point at them.

mission.setup: Mia, Sam and Smarty look at pictures of the year. Talk about the first months and what you like.

turns.smarty: It is cold in January. Do you like January?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

turns.smarty: What do you like? January, March or May?
turns.hint: Say I like + a month.

lessons.title: June to October
lessons.scenario: Leo, Ana and Smarty are at the beach. They talk about the summer months and about school.

items.note: June comes after May.
July comes after June.
August comes after July.

items.example: I go to school in September.
items.note: September comes after August.
October comes after September.

practice.prompt: Which month comes in the middle?
practice.explanation: The order is May, June, July.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the month at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I go to school in September.
practice.explanation: We use in before a month.

practice.prompt: Match each month with the month that comes next.
practice.explanation: Each month has a next month.

practice.prompt: Type a month for swimming.
practice.explanation: These months are warm for swimming.

practice.prompt: Which month comes before June?
practice.explanation: May comes before June.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: We go to the beach in July.
practice.explanation: We go to the beach in a hot month.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for rains and for April.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Say it slowly: It is sunny in August.

story.hook: Who likes the beach in July?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I like the beach in July.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I like the beach in August.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I go to school in September.

questions.prompt: Who goes to school in September?
questions.explanation: Leo says: I go to school in September.

questions.prompt: Who likes the beach in July?
questions.explanation: Ana says: I like the beach in July.
Leo says: It is hot in July.

image.describe: A sunny beach with sand and blue water. Leo, Ana and Smarty the black cat sit on towels with a beach umbrella; a school bag lies next to Leo.

mission.setup: Leo, Ana and Smarty are at the beach. They talk about the summer months and about school.

turns.smarty: I like the beach in July. And you?
turns.hint: Say a month you like. For example: I like June.

turns.smarty: Do you go to school in July?
accept: ^i do not go to school in (?:january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october)$
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

lessons.title: My birthday
lessons.scenario: It is Mia's birthday. Sam, Ben and Smarty are at her party. Talk about birthdays and months.

items.note: November comes after October.
December is the last month of the year.

items.example: There are twelve months in a year.
items.note: A year has twelve months.
A year has twelve months. We use years to say how old someone is.
Say: My birthday is in + a month, to tell when your birthday is.

image.describe: A birthday cake with candles on a table, with Smarty the black cat wearing a party hat and balloons behind.

practice.prompt: Which month comes in the middle?
practice.explanation: The order is October, November, December.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: There are twelve ___ in a year.
practice.explanation: A year has twelve months.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the month at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use in before a month.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its plural.
practice.explanation: Add -s to talk about more than one.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: How old are you? Choose an answer.
practice.explanation: How old asks for a number of years.

practice.prompt: Say it to Mia on her special day.
practice.explanation: We say Happy birthday on someone's birthday.

practice.prompt: Mia says: My birthday is in July. Which month is it?
practice.explanation: Mia says July.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: You can say your own month, too.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Years old tells how old you are.

questions.explanation: Mia says: I am twelve years old.

questions.prompt: Who has a birthday in December?
questions.explanation: Ben says: My birthday is in December.
Smarty says: Happy birthday, Mia!

image.describe: A birthday party in a living room: Mia blows out candles on a big cake while Sam, Ben and Smarty the black cat clap, with a table of juice and cups.

mission.setup: It is Mia's birthday. Sam, Ben and Smarty are at her party. Talk about birthdays and months.

turns.smarty: My birthday is in May. And you?
turns.hint: Say My birthday is in + a month. You can use an imaginary month.

turns.smarty: Happy birthday! How old are you?
turns.hint: Say I am + a number. You can use an imaginary age.

lessons.title: I'm going to visit
lessons.scenario: Leo, Ana and Smarty stand at the door of the garage. Talk about what you are going to do tomorrow and next week.

items.note: Use "I'm going to" and a verb to talk about your plans.

items.example: I am going to swim tomorrow.
items.note: Tomorrow means the next day.

items.example: I am going to visit Mia next week.
items.note: Next week means in the week after this one.

items.example: I am going to visit my aunt.
items.note: Visit means to go and see a person or a place.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and a girl at the front door of a friend's house; the friend opens the door and waves.

grammar.title: Plans with going to
grammar.explanation: Use I am going to + a verb to talk about a plan. I'm is the short form of I am.
examples: I'm going to visit Mia tomorrow.

practice.prompt: You want to say what you will do tomorrow.
practice.answer: I am going to swim tomorrow.
options: I am going to swim tomorrow.
practice.explanation: Use going to for a plan. Now and every day are not plans for tomorrow.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: I am going to visit my aunt.
practice.answer: I am going to visit my aunt.
options: I am going to visit my aunt.
I am going to visit my uncle.
I am going to visit my cousin.
practice.explanation: Listen for the person at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am going to visit Mia next week.
practice.explanation: Put next week at the end.

practice.prompt: Type a verb for your plan.
practice.explanation: After going to we use a verb.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I am going to swim tomorrow.
practice.answer: I am going to swim tomorrow.
practice.explanation: Say it slowly. You can say another plan, too.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: He is going to ___ his aunt.
practice.explanation: We visit a person. We do not eat or wash an aunt.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: We are going to the beach tomorrow.
practice.explanation: Use we are for more than one person.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: I am going to cook dinner tomorrow.
practice.answer: I am going to cook dinner tomorrow.
options: I am going to cook dinner tomorrow.
I am going to cook lunch tomorrow.
I am going to cook dinner next week.
practice.explanation: Listen for the meal and for the time.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I am going to visit the ___ next week.
practice.explanation: We visit places like a museum.

practice.prompt: Ben says: I am going to visit my cousin next week. Who is Ben going to visit?
practice.explanation: Ben says cousin.

story.hook: Who is going to swim tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: What are you going to do tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I am going to visit my grandmother.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Nice! I am going to swim tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I am going to visit Mia next week.

questions.prompt: Who is going to swim tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Leo says: I am going to swim tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Who is going to visit a grandmother?
questions.explanation: Ana says: I am going to visit my grandmother.

questions.prompt: When is Smarty going to visit Mia?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I am going to visit Mia next week.

image.describe: The open door of a garage with a bike and a suitcase inside. Leo and Ana talk outside while Smarty the black cat looks at a family house across the road.

mission.setup: Leo, Ana and Smarty stand at the door of the garage. Talk about what you are going to do tomorrow and next week.

turns.smarty: What are you going to do tomorrow?
turns.hint: Say I am going to + a verb. For example: I am going to swim.

turns.smarty: And what are you going to do next week?
turns.example: I am going to visit my aunt.
turns.hint: Say I am going to + a verb.

turns.smarty: I am going to visit Mia. Are you going to visit a friend?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I am or No, I am not.

lessons.title: Holidays
lessons.scenario: Omar and Zara talk about a holiday. Smarty listens. Talk about holidays, hotels and passports.

items.example: I am going to have a holiday.
items.note: A holiday is time away from school or work. You can say: I love my holiday.

image.describe: A happy family and Smarty the black cat on a sunny beach with towels, a sandcastle and a beach umbrella.

items.note: A hotel is a place with many rooms where people sleep on holiday.

image.describe: A tall hotel building with a sign shape, balconies and a swimming pool; Smarty the black cat waits at the door with a small suitcase.

items.example: My passport is in my bag.
items.note: You show your passport when you travel to another country.

image.describe: A small blue passport book lying open on a table next to a pen, with Smarty the black cat looking at it.

items.note: Use travel to say you go to a place far away. Say: I travel by plane.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A passport is small and fits in a bag. A hotel does not.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the size word at the end.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence about how you travel.
practice.explanation: Say by + the vehicle.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its plural or -s form.
practice.explanation: Add -s for more than one, or for he and she.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I am going to ___ by train.
practice.explanation: After going to we use a verb: travel.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am going to travel next week.
practice.explanation: Next week goes at the end.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the month at the end.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: You can say you love your holiday.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We are going to visit the ___ tomorrow.
practice.explanation: We visit places like a museum.

story.hook: How is Omar going to travel?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Hello, Zara! My holiday is next week.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Great! Are you going to travel by plane?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes, I am. I have my passport.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Is the hotel near the beach?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes, it is. It is big and beautiful.

questions.prompt: How is Omar going to travel?
questions.explanation: Omar says Yes, I am to travel by plane.
Omar says: I have my passport.
Zara asks about the hotel and Omar says it is near.

image.describe: A bright living room with a suitcase and a passport on the table. Omar and Zara talk while Smarty the black cat looks at a picture of a hotel by the beach on the wall.

mission.setup: Omar and Zara talk about a holiday. Smarty listens. Talk about holidays, hotels and passports.

turns.smarty: Do you like holidays?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

turns.smarty: I am going to travel by plane next week. And you?
turns.example: I am going to travel by train.
turns.hint: Say I am going to travel by + a vehicle.

turns.smarty: Do you have a passport?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

lessons.title: Where are you going?
lessons.scenario: Mia meets Tom with a suitcase. Ask where he is going and when the plane leaves.

items.note: Ask "Where are you going?" to find out someone's plan. Answer: I'm going to + a place.

items.example: I am going to the airport.
items.note: An airport is a place where planes arrive and leave.

image.describe: A busy airport hall with a big window showing a plane; Smarty the black cat sits on a suitcase and watches a board with arrows.

items.note: Arrive means to get to a place.

items.example: The train leaves at six o'clock.
items.note: Leave means to go away from a place.

practice.prompt: Ben asks: Where are you going? You are going to the airport. What do you say?
practice.answer: I am going to the airport.
options: I am going to the airport.
I am going to the park.
I am going to the school.
practice.explanation: Answer with I am going to + the place.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Going is the word that asks about a plan.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.explanation: Where + are you + going asks about a place you will go.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A train can leave or arrive at a time. A train does not sleep or eat.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: The plane leaves at eight o'clock.
practice.explanation: Use at before the time.

practice.prompt: You want to find the airport. Choose the question.
practice.answer: Excuse me, where is the airport?
options: Excuse me, where is the airport?
Excuse me, where is the school?
Excuse me, where is the hospital?
practice.explanation: Say the name of the place you need.

practice.prompt: Match each question with an answer.

pairs.right: I am going to the airport.

practice.explanation: Each question needs the right kind of answer.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: I am going to the airport.
practice.answer: I am going to the airport.
options: I am going to the airport.
I am going to the station.
I am going to the park.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place at the end.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud.
practice.explanation: Say it with a friendly voice.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ at the airport at two o'clock.
practice.explanation: You arrive at a place when you get there.

story.hook: What time does the plane leave?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hi, Tom! Where are you going?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I am going to the airport.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, it leaves at ten o'clock.

questions.explanation: Tom says: I am going to the airport.

questions.prompt: What time does the plane leave?
questions.explanation: Tom says it leaves at ten o'clock.

questions.prompt: How is Tom going to the airport?
questions.explanation: Mia asks about the taxi and Tom says it is here.

image.describe: Outside a house, Tom pulls a suitcase towards a yellow taxi. Mia waves from the door and Smarty the black cat watches from the garden wall.

mission.setup: Mia meets Tom with a suitcase. Ask where he is going and when the plane leaves.

turns.smarty: Hi! Where are you going?
turns.example: I am going to the park.
turns.hint: Say I am going to + a place. For example: I am going to the park.

turns.smarty: Do you travel by plane or by train?
turns.hint: Say by plane or by train. You can also say I travel by + a vehicle.

lessons.title: Packing
lessons.canDo: Say what you need for a trip
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam are in the garage with suitcases. Mia is going to travel. Talk about what to pack and what she needs.

items.note: Pack means to put your things into a bag or a suitcase.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat packs a hat and a camera into an open suitcase while a child folds clothes next to it.

items.note: You use a camera to take photos.

image.describe: A black digital camera with a big round lens held by Smarty the black cat who looks through it.

items.note: You wear sunglasses when it is sunny. The word sunglasses is always plural.

image.describe: A pair of round dark sunglasses on the nose of Smarty the black cat on a sunny beach.

items.note: Use need to say what you must have. Say: I need my passport.

grammar.title: Need
grammar.explanation: Use need to say what you must have. Use needs after he, she and it.

practice.prompt: Type something you need for a trip.
practice.explanation: These things are useful on a trip.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the thing at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Pack goes before the thing you put in.

practice.prompt: It is sunny and hot. What do you need?
practice.explanation: Gloves and a scarf are for cold weather.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its -s form.
practice.explanation: Add -s for he, she and it, or for more than one.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I am going to ___ my suitcase tomorrow.
practice.explanation: You pack a suitcase before a trip.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I need my passport and my camera.
practice.explanation: Use and to join two things.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Say it slowly.

practice.prompt: Ana is going to the beach. What does she need?
practice.explanation: Use needs after she. A beach day is sunny.

story.hook: What does Mia need for her trip?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Mia! Are you going to travel?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Yes, I am. I am going to pack my suitcase now.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I need my passport and my camera.

questions.explanation: Mia says: I am going to pack my suitcase.
Mia says: I need my passport and my camera.
Sam says: Pack your sunglasses, too!

image.describe: A garage with open suitcases on the floor. Mia puts a camera and a passport in one suitcase while Sam holds up sunglasses and Smarty the black cat sits inside a bag.

mission.setup: Mia and Sam are in the garage with suitcases. Mia is going to travel. Talk about what to pack and what she needs.

turns.smarty: What do you need for a holiday?
turns.hint: Say I need + a thing. For example: I need my camera.

turns.smarty: Do you have a camera?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

turns.smarty: I need my sunglasses. Do you need sunglasses?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I do or No, I do not.

lessons.title: How long?
lessons.canDo: Ask how long a trip is
lessons.scenario: Ben and Ana talk about a trip. Ask how long it is and talk about a souvenir.

items.note: Ask "How long?" to find the time of something. Answer: It is ten minutes.
A trip is a time when you go to a place and come back.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and a child walking along a sunny road with backpacks and a map, a hill and a river ahead.

items.example: A trip by train is fun.
items.note: Fun means that you enjoy it. Say: It is fun!
A souvenir is a small thing you buy on a trip to remember it.

image.describe: A small snow globe and a little toy model of a tower on a shop shelf; Smarty the black cat holds one in his paws.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the word after How.

practice.prompt: Complete the question.
practice.text: How ___ is the trip? It is ten minutes.
practice.explanation: Ten minutes is a time, so we ask How long.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use one + a time word to say how long.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I buy a ___ in the shop.
practice.explanation: You can buy a souvenir in a shop.

practice.prompt: Match each question with an answer.
practice.explanation: The word after How tells you the kind of answer.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud.
practice.explanation: Say it clearly.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Minutes is a short time.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.audio: A trip by train is fun.
practice.answer: A trip by train is fun.
options: A trip by train is fun.
A trip by plane is fun.
A trip by boat is fun.
practice.explanation: Listen for the vehicle.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am going to buy a souvenir.
practice.explanation: Use going to for a plan.

story.hook: What is Ben going to buy?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I am going to visit my cousin.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I am going to buy a souvenir for you.

questions.prompt: Who is going to visit a cousin?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I am going to visit my cousin.
Ben says: It is one week.

questions.prompt: What is Ben going to buy?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I am going to buy a souvenir.

image.describe: A garage table with a map and a suitcase. Ben and Ana talk happily, while Smarty the black cat holds a small toy souvenir in his paws.

mission.setup: Ben and Ana talk about a trip. Ask how long it is and talk about a souvenir.

turns.smarty: How long is your trip?
turns.hint: Say a time. For example: It is one week.

turns.smarty: A trip is fun! Are you going to buy a souvenir?
accept: ^i am going to buy a souvenir$
turns.hint: Say Yes, I am or No, I am not.

lessons.title: The big trip
lessons.scenario: Zara is going to travel and Omar says goodbye. Plan a trip with Smarty and say a friendly goodbye.

items.note: Say "Have a good trip!" to a friend who is going to travel.
Say "See you soon" when you will meet again in a short time.
A postcard is a card with a picture that you send from a trip.

image.describe: A colourful postcard with a picture of a sunny beach, lying on a table next to a pen; Smarty the black cat looks at it.

items.note: Use enjoy to say you like doing something. Say: Enjoy your holiday!

practice.prompt: Your friend is going to travel. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Say Have a good trip before someone travels.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for soon and for the name.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Have a good trip is a friendly phrase for a traveller.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I buy a ___ at the shop.
practice.explanation: You can buy a postcard at a shop.

practice.prompt: Match each line with a reply.

pairs.right: I am going to the airport.

practice.explanation: A friendly line often has a friendly reply.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am going to visit my cousin next week.
practice.explanation: Use going to for a plan.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
